overview: Senegal's women's health innovation ecosystem is anchored in maternal, reproductive and cervical-cancer care, supported by a fast-maturing digital-health push led by the government. Homegrown startups such as Njureel (teleconsultation and reproductive-health education) and Askcare (low-cost cervical-cancer screening) operate alongside a national e-health strategy validated in 2025 and a sovereign-backed fund, Oyass Capital, financing healthtech infrastructure. Gender-lens capital is unusually visible for the region, led by Dakar-based WIC Capital and Janngo Capital. The state has cut maternal mortality sharply since 2017 while pushing a Shared Single Patient Record and pending e-health legislation.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent activity clusters around digital-health funding and cervical-cancer innovation.

items.text: Eyone Medical raises USD 3M from FONSIS-backed Oyass Capital to digitise health records across Francophone West Africa.
Eyone Medical secures a further CFA 1bn (USD 1.7M) from Oyass Capital to roll out Senegal's Shared Single Patient Record (DPUP).
Ministry of Health's Digital Health Unit announces a bill to regulate e-health services in Senegal.
Senegal launches the CAAP initiative to advance women's, children's and adolescents' health.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: A national digital-health framework and reproductive-health strategy set the direction.

items.text: Senegal validates its National Digital Health Strategy (Strategie Nationale de Sante Numerique) with roughly USD 50M in World Bank support.
SRMNIA-N Strategic Plan 2024-2028 commits to accelerating reductions in maternal, neonatal and adolescent mortality, with action plans for family planning and adolescent reproductive health.
National Family Planning Action Plan launched, built on the '3 Ds' (democratise, demedicalise, decentralise) in response to the Ouagadougou Call to Action.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Startups and hubs are building reproductive-health and digital-care services.

items.text: Njureel scales its Sama Bajene reproductive-health programme, reporting 60+ trained community health workers, 500+ consultations and 800+ women reached.
Askcare expands its '3T' cervical-cancer model (HPV test, AI colposcope, thermo-ablation) across a network of 80+ centres in Senegal, plus Rwanda and Nigeria.
Eyone Medical's Shared Patient Record platform now runs in 60+ healthcare institutions across Senegal, Mali, Cote d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Gabon and France.
Lafiya Innovators runs a health-tech incubation Starter Track in Dakar for early-stage health startups.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: A mix of women's-health startups, digital-health firms, incubators and government bodies.

items.name: Askcare Femtech
items.note: Low-cost, AI-assisted cervical-cancer screening & treatment; founded by Aissatou Diallo.

items.name: Njureel
items.note: Teleconsultation & reproductive-health platform; runs the Sama Bajene women's-health education programme.

items.name: Sama Bajene
items.note: Helps health facilities manage services/appointments to reduce maternal mortality; supports women victims of violence.

items.name: Eyone Medical
items.note: Interoperable digital-health records; powers Senegal's Shared Single Patient Record. Founded 2015.

items.name: CTIC Dakar
items.note: First ICT startup incubator/accelerator in Francophone Sub-Saharan Africa (est. 2011).

items.name: Lafiya Innovators (Impact Hub Dakar)
items.note: Health-tech incubation programme with a Dakar-based Starter Track.

items.name: Ministry of Health & Social Action, Digital Health Unit
items.note: Drives the National Digital Health Strategy and pending e-health regulation.

items.name: Association Sante Mobile (Dakar)
items.note: Addresses menstrual hygiene and reproductive health for girls and women.

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Senegal has notable sovereign-backed and gender-lens capital for health and women-led ventures.

items.name: Oyass Capital
items.role: FONSIS-backed fund; USD 3M+ into healthtech Eyone Medical for digital health infrastructure.

items.name: WIC Capital
items.role: First Francophone West Africa fund dedicated to women-led businesses; USD 20M, equity & quasi-equity.

items.name: Janngo Capital
items.role: Pan-African, gender-balanced VC led by Fatoumata Ba; healthcare among target sectors; EUR 73M fund II.

items.name: FONSIS (Senegal sovereign wealth fund)
items.role: Parent of Oyass Capital, financing high-impact SMEs including health.

items.name: UNICEF Femtech Ventures
items.role: Five-year (2025-2030) platform giving equity-free capital up to USD 100k to women's-health startups; over half of 1,100+ applicants from Africa.
